title: Inputs Define Outputs
equation: Output Quality = Input Quality × Process Quality
hook: You can have a great process and still get bad results if what's going into it is junk.
statement: Garbage in, garbage out applies to everything you do.
explainer: Bad leads, bad info, bad materials. A great process can't save them. It's usually cheaper to fix what goes in than to keep patching what comes out.
sop: List every input feeding one key result, like leads, info, or materials.
Score the Input Quality of each source 1 to 10.
Cut the lowest one, even if it's the cheapest.
Write down a minimum quality bar for that input.
Re-check every quarter, because bad sources creep back in.
equation_example: Input Quality 4, Process Quality 9. 4 × 9 = 36 out of 100. Higher means both are strong. Lower, even with a great process, means bad inputs are capping what you can produce.
question: Name one low-quality input you put up with every day and decide what replaces it.
closing_statement: Protect what goes in before you fix what comes out.
caption:
Principle Nº 102: Inputs Define Outputs

You can have a great process and still get bad results if what's going into it is junk.

Garbage in, garbage out applies to everything you do.

Your turn: Name one low-quality input you put up with every day and decide what replaces it.
